messages.text: You've got 33 gaps across the three papers in the workspace — Attention Is All You Need, Improved DDPM, and Mamba. By kind: nine caveats (label smoothing hurting perplexity, DDIM likelihood never evaluated, cosine-schedule choices), seven limitations (mostly around Mamba — the attention compatibility function, incomplete long-context baselines, undisclosed engineering challenges), seven future-work items (non-text modalities, Mamba's downstream affordances and video applications), five assumptions (sinusoidal encodings and extrapolation, the selection mechanism), three negative results, and two threats to validity. Which one would you like me to load and work from? If nothing jumps out, the DDIM-likelihood gap or the Mamba scaling questions look like the most actionable.
Can you tell me what 3 gaps are close to each otherß

The closest trio is three Mamba gaps that are really the same worry stated three ways: "Evaluation limited to small model sizes", "Whether Mamba maintains advantage at larger parameter scales", and "Scaling may involve undisclosed engineering challenges" — all of them say Mamba has only been tested small and whether it holds up at scale is open. The next tightest cluster is about the attention mechanism itself: the dot-product compatibility function, reduced effective resolution from averaging, and local restricted attention for large inputs. There's a third around DDPM likelihood: DDIM likelihood never evaluated, hybrid objectives sacrificing optimal log-likelihood, and NLL scaling not following a clean power law. Want me to work from one of these trios — for example, bundle the three Mamba scaling gaps into a single candidate idea?
